\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Small-set center of mass]
\lean{FABL.smallSetCenterOfMass}
\statementsource{vershynin-hdp-book}{
  pdf-681b6f3d947f-p010-b003,
  pdf-681b6f3d947f-p010-b004
}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p139-b005}
\label{FABL.smallSetCenterOfMass}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.signValue}
For $n\in\mathbb N$, a function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and $\alpha\in\mathbb R$,
define a vector in $\mathbb R^n$ whose $i$th coordinate is $\mathbb
E_x[f(x)x_i]/\alpha$, where $x$ is uniformly distributed on the Boolean cube.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Coordinates of the center of mass]
\lean{FABL.smallSetCenterOfMass_apply}
\label{FABL.smallSetCenterOfMass_apply}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.monomial, FABL.smallSetCenterOfMass}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$, let $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$,
and let $i$ be a coordinate. The $i$th coordinate of the center of mass defined by $f$
and $\alpha$ equals the singleton Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $\{i\}$ divided by
$\alpha$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Center-of-mass squared norm]
\lean{FABL.sum_sq_smallSetCenterOfMass}
\label{FABL.sum_sq_smallSetCenterOfMass}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel_one_eq_sum_singleton, FABL.smallSetCenterOfMass, FABL.smallSetCenterOfMass_apply}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $\alpha\in\mathbb
R$. The sum of the squares of the coordinates of the small-set center of mass of $f$ at
scale $\alpha$ equals the level-one Fourier weight of $f$ divided by $\alpha^2$. At
$\alpha=0$, both sides are zero under the usual totalized real division convention.
\end{theorem}
